I am an old woman, seventy years now, and this small maize plot behind my house is only a tiny piece — less than a quarter of a timad. I have no money to buy the fertilizer from the cooperative, and one bag is far too much for such a small plot anyway. I will put the manure from my few animals like I always do, and save my own seed from last harvest like my mother taught me. My grandchildren help me weed, and my own two hands still work — I do not hire anyone, I have no cash for that.
